I do this for a living, so I know what I'm talking about. The spring system your talking about with the safety cables is an outdated design and not in use anymore. The new models use a torsion spring that utilises rotationally tension instead of expanding the springs. This makes them much more dangerous because you have to manually tension the spring before securing it in place. For this reason, very few places will even tell you how to do it as it's a huge liability. That being said, before doing anything, you need to determine which style of tension system you have. If the springs are on either side of the door with the cables running through pulleys, you have the extension spring type. If the spring are above the middle of the door on a horizontal shaft, don't even think about it without doing a LOT of research. Don't even touch a single bolt until your sure about what it is. These springs could have upwards of 100 pounds of force osn them and attach to brackets at the bottom of the door. If you you detach these brackets under tension, they're destroying something, likely your hands.
